# git: alias: please doesn't respect tracking state

Make `git please` push to the branch's configured upstream, not to a same-named branch on every remote:

```
  for remote in $(git remote | grep -Ev '^(upstream|fork-.*)$'); do
    git push --force-with-lease --tags "${remote}" "$(git current)"
  done
```

The author's forks of [octolab/.github](https://github.com/octolab/.github) have branches tracking different remotes (branch `lifeos` → remote `fork-lifeos`, with `upstream` as the parent). `git please` iterated over the remotes and force-pushed the current branch name to each, so a branch meant for a fork overwrote history on `origin`. Labelled critical.
